lead: Object-oriented, web and mobile systems fail in ways that plain functions do not. An object can dispatch to a subclass, a web page depends on a session stored on a server, and a mobile app loses the network when a call arrives. This chapter shows tests that follow those mechanisms: class trees for OO code, browser and session paths for web apps, and device plus network conditions for mobile apps. The ideas extend the functional test design from Chapters 3 and 4 and the configuration testing from Chapter 8.
prereq: You need: Chapter 4.1 for test cases, 4.4 for input partitions, 4.5 for unit and integration levels, and Unit 3 UML class diagrams for inheritance.

sections.h3: Object-oriented testing follows the class tree

blocks.text: Some syllabi call this testing OO systems and website testing; the tests still follow the same mechanisms. Object-oriented testing checks a method, a class, a cluster of classes and the whole system. Method testing is unit testing of one operation. Class testing checks all methods plus the object's state. Cluster testing checks classes that collaborate. System testing checks the complete OO product. See 4.5 for the unit and integration levels.

Inheritance means a subclass gets methods from its parent and may override them. A test suite for a subclass must run all inherited tests that still apply, then its own tests. Testing only the base class misses changes in the child.

Polymorphism means a variable of base type can hold any subclass object. One call can run different methods. Test each actual type, not just the base type. The figure shows Payment with subclasses UPI and Card.

State-based testing is for objects with memory. Test a legal sequence and an illegal sequence. A payment object must not pay twice after a timeout. Use the state chart from Unit 3 to list states and events.

sections.h3: Web tests cover content, links, forms and sessions

blocks.text: A web app splits into the browser page, server code and a database. A web test must check content, links, forms, cookies and sessions, navigation, browser compatibility, basic security and performance.

items: Content: text, price and currency are correct.
Links: no broken link and no wrong destination.
Forms: mandatory fields, field rules and boundary values from 4.4.
Cookies and session: HTTP has no memory, so the server sends a cookie with a session id. Test login, logout, timeout, back button and two tabs.
Navigation: back, forward and refresh must not repeat a payment or show stale data.
Browser compatibility: run the same tests on Chrome and Firefox, and on the versions you support.
Security basics: validate input, keep passwords out of URLs, and do not expose the session id.
Performance: use 4.8 for load and stress tests.

sections.h3: Mobile tests cover device, network and interruption

blocks.text: A mobile app runs on many devices and OS versions. Use a device and OS matrix. Test high-risk combinations, not every device. A ₹500 payment may work on one phone and fail on another with low memory.

items: Network: Wi-Fi, 4G, weak signal and lost network during payment. Check retry and no double debit.
Interruptions: incoming call, SMS, notification, battery low, low memory, screen rotation, background and foreground.
Location: permission denied, stale GPS and no GPS.
Install and update: fresh install, upgrade with old data and uninstall.
Usability: touch target size, font size, offline message and error recovery.

blocks.text: Configuration testing from 4.8 gives the matrix method. A device is a configuration; each scenario with input and expected result is a test.

figure.caption: The base class Payment declares pay(amount); UPI and Card extend it and override pay. A call through a Payment variable can run either override, so test both actual types.

spec.aria: A directed graph shows Payment as the base class with UPI and Card as subclasses that override pay.

examples.question: A payment system has base class Payment with method pay(amount). UPI and Card extend Payment and override pay(). A test creates Payment[] p = {new UPI(), new Card()}; p[0].pay(₹500) must use UPI and p[1].pay(₹500) must use Card. A web login form is tested on Chrome and Firefox with one valid login and one wrong password. A mobile app is tested on 4 devices with network lost once during a ₹500 payment. Write one OO test, one web test and one mobile test. Count the concrete test cases.
steps: OO polymorphism: there are 2 actual types, UPI and Card. Case 1 calls p[0].pay(500) and checks that UPI.pay ran. Case 2 calls p[1].pay(500) and checks that Card.pay ran. Count = 2.
Web login: browsers = 2 (Chrome, Firefox). Form cases = 2 (valid login, wrong password). Web cases = 2 × 2 = 4. On each browser, a valid login must create a session cookie; a wrong password must not.
Mobile payment: devices = 4. Network-loss cases per device = 1. Mobile cases = 4 × 1 = 4. For each device, cut the network after the ₹500 request; expect an error or retry and only one debit.
examples.answer: The example gives 2 OO polymorphism cases, 4 web login cases and 4 mobile network-loss cases, for 10 concrete test cases in total.
examples.check:
oo_types = 2
browsers = 2
form_cases = 2
devices = 4
network_loss_cases = 1
web = browsers * form_cases
mobile = devices * network_loss_cases
total = oo_types + web + mobile
print(oo_types)
print(web)
print(mobile)
print(total)

traps: Testing only the base class and not each subclass. The override in UPI or Card can fail while Payment passes.
Treating polymorphism as one test. One call can run different methods; test each actual type that the variable can hold.
On web, checking only that the page loads. Test form rules, session cookie, logout, timeout and the back button.
On mobile, testing one device on Wi-Fi only. Add network loss during payment and at least one interruption such as a call.
Counting a device or browser as a test without input and expected result. A device is a configuration; a scenario is a test.

quiz.q: Define method testing, class testing, cluster testing and system testing for OO software.
quiz.a: Method testing checks one operation. Class testing checks all methods plus object state. Cluster testing checks collaborating classes. System testing checks the complete OO product.

quiz.q: Why must a subclass test suite include inherited tests?
quiz.a: The subclass inherits behaviour that users still depend on. If the subclass changes shared state or overrides a method, old base behaviour can break. Inherited tests catch that regression; subclass tests add new behaviour.

quiz.q: Payment is the base class. UPI and Card override pay(). An array holds one UPI object and one Card object. How many polymorphism test cases are needed for pay(₹500), and what does each assert?
quiz.a: Two cases. Case 1 calls pay(500) on the UPI object and asserts UPI.pay ran. Case 2 calls pay(500) on the Card object and asserts Card.pay ran. A base-only test does not prove either override.

quiz.q: A login form is tested on 3 browsers with 2 form cases: valid login and wrong password. How many web test cases are there?
quiz.a: 3 browsers × 2 form cases = 6 web test cases. Each valid login must create a session cookie; each wrong password must not.

quiz.q: A mobile payment app fails only on 4G during payment. Which test conditions should be added?
quiz.a: Add network handover from Wi-Fi to 4G, weak 4G signal, network loss after the request, and retry after reconnection. Check one debit only, clear error message and no duplicate payment.

quiz.q: Why is testing a web app on Chrome only and a mobile app on one Android device risky?
quiz.a: Browser engines and device OS versions differ in JavaScript, layout, permissions, memory and network handling. A path that works on one configuration can fail on another. Use a small risk-based matrix, not one configuration.

quiz.q: What is state-based testing for an object?
quiz.a: It tests sequences of calls that change the object's state. Test a legal sequence and an illegal sequence, such as paying twice after a timeout, using a state chart.
Login creates a session, logout ends it, timeout ends it, and the back button after logout must not show protected data. Also check that a second tab uses the same session correctly.

beyond: Not for the exam. Industry uses model-based testing for state machines, cloud device farms for mobile matrices, and session fuzzing for web apps. Search terms: state transition testing, Selenium WebDriver, Appium, device farm, contract testing for APIs. Research grows on flaky test detection in browser and mobile suites.
